parties:
MD.AMIRUL ISLAM
Vs.
MD.SHAHABUDDIN AND OTHERS.
full_judgment: 10. The submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners is of no substance since as per Section 95 (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 an usufructuary mortgage is required to be registered one. Admittedly the Kabala sought to be pre-empted was a sale deed. In the Kabala there is no stipulation for re-conveyance. The contention of the pre-emptees that the transfer sought to be pre-empted was not a sale but an usufructuary mortgage is based on an un-registered deed of agreement for re-conveyance. In the background of the facts of the case the Appellate Judge has observed that the alleged deed of re-conveyance was brought into existence upon an unholy alliance between the pre-emptees and the seller only to frustrate the claim of pre-emption. Since there was no registered deed of usufructuary mortgage in respect of the land sought to be pre-empted and that the deed of agreement for re-conveyance is an unregistered one, in my opinion the observation that has been made by the Appellate Court as to the nature of the deed of re-conveyance cannot be said to be of no basis.
